units.source: Say who or what you have

units.context: Scenario: Family · Lesson: Introducing Your Family · grammar (Subject + 有 + Object)
units.source: "有" states that something exists or that you have it - it's the verb used for "there is/are" and "I have".
units.translation: "有" indica que algo existe o que lo tienes: es el verbo que se usa para "hay" y para "tengo".

units.context: Scenario: Family · Lesson: Introducing Your Family · grammar (Subject + 有 + Object)
units.source: Using 是 instead of 有: "我家有四口人" is correct, not "我家是四口人".
units.translation: Usar 是 en vez de 有: lo correcto es "我家有四口人", no "我家是四口人".

units.context: Scenario: Family · Lesson: Introducing Your Family · grammar (几 + 口 + 人)
units.source: "口" is the measure word used specifically for counting family members; "几口人" asks how many people are in a family.
units.translation: "口" es el clasificador que se usa específicamente para contar miembros de la familia; "几口人" pregunta cuántas personas hay en una familia.

units.context: Scenario: Family · Lesson: Introducing Your Family · grammar (几 + 口 + 人)
units.source: Using 个 instead of 口 for family members - 口 is the natural choice here, even though 个 is heard casually elsewhere.
units.translation: Usar 个 en vez de 口 para los miembros de la familia: 口 es la opción natural aquí, aunque 个 se oiga de forma casual en otros contextos.

units.source: "岁" is the word for "years old" - it comes directly after the number.

units.context: Scenario: Family · Lesson: Describing Family Members · grammar (Subject + (很) + Adjective)
units.source: In Chinese, an adjective can be the whole predicate by itself; 很 softens it into a neutral description rather than a strong "very". 是 is not used before an adjective.
units.translation: En chino, un adjetivo puede ser todo el predicado por sí solo; 很 lo suaviza para que sea una descripción neutra en vez de un "muy" enfático. 是 no se usa antes de un adjetivo.

units.context: Scenario: Family · Lesson: Describing Family Members · grammar (Subject + (很) + Adjective)
units.source: Saying "他是很高" instead of "他很高" - 是 doesn't belong before an adjective predicate.
units.translation: Decir "他是很高" en vez de "他很高": 是 no va antes de un predicado adjetival.
